title: Bbox re-extract changed spawn_candidates + districts, forcing a dublin_board T1 (sim state-hash) golden re-bless beyond the 'board-underlay only' scope
evidence: osm_extract.py:75 `BBOX = (53.30, -6.32, 53.385, -6.08)` (diff removes `BBOX = (53.28, -6.45, 53.44, -6.03)`). `git diff v2..HEAD --stat -- goldens/` shows `goldens/dublin_board.t1 | 3602 +++++++++++++++++++-------------------`; goldens/dublin_board.t1 header: `# t1 manifest — per-tick FNV-1a-64 state hashes (full sim state)`. Measured asset deltas: spawn_candidates 224,646 -> 125,860; districts 121 -> 52.
detail: Briefing rule: 'Spawn candidates/district data unchanged (gameplay semantics pin) — this is a RENDER/DATA-STYLING change, not a sim change' and 'goldens re-bless ONLY the board-underlay class'. The T1 sim-state golden changed, i.e. Dublin gameplay itself changed. Mitigation: commit cites a 2026-08-24 mock-gate user ruling approving the tight bbox.
recommended_fix: Either re-extract at the county bbox to re-pin the pool, or record the core-bbox ruling as a formal spec amendment and bless-cause entry covering the T1 re-bless.

title: Irish Sea is clipped to a 1300 m coastal strip; the far-east board renders as paper where open sea should be
evidence: osm_extract.py:483 `sea = sea.intersection(coast_union.buffer(SEA_STRIP_M))`; osm_extract.py:100 `SEA_STRIP_M = 1300.0`; comment line 96: `# The sea strip: the open-sea face is clipped to a ~4-tile coastal band`. Measured pixels of the committed underlay: (0.97W, 0.25H) = (178,204,223) ~ WATER (179,205,224); (0.97W, 0.5H) = (237,226,200) = exact CANVAS paper.
detail: Briefing AC: 'the IRISH SEA renders as water' / 'the eastern board must be WATER ... render the sea as the big flat body it is'. Beyond the strip the eastern edge reads as beige land. Code cites a later user ruling ('maybe just 10%') not present in the briefing.
recommended_fix: Extend the sea fill east of the coastline to the bbox edge (full eastern band), or record the coastal-strip ruling in the spec as the accepted sea treatment.

title: dublin_node_block_draw logs every frame despite the claimed 'one-shot log line'; per-frame console I/O in the world draw path
evidence: dublin.odin:53-55 comment: `// an axis-aligned block + a one-shot log line (amendment #2: flag, never` / `// silently float).`; dublin.odin:336 `fmt.printfln("[dublin] node at (%.1f, %.1f) has no street within %.0f tiles - axis-aligned block", tx, ty, DUBLIN_SEG_MAX_DIST)` — inside dublin_node_block_draw, called per terminal per frame from view.odin:1122 `top_y := dublin_node_block_draw(v, c, fam, reveal_scale)` with no latch.
detail: Comment claims one-shot; code prints on every call — 60 log lines/sec per far-from-street node for the rest of a run. Violates the project rule 'no per-frame work... zero per-frame heap churn' and pollures harness capture runs.
recommended_fix: Latch the flag: log once per node id (or once per board build) instead of inside the per-frame draw; keep the axis-aligned fallback behavior.

title: Dublin terminal path silently drops reveal_fade — spawn reveal pops instead of fading on the restyled board
evidence: view.odin:1122 `top_y := dublin_node_block_draw(v, c, fam, reveal_scale)` — reveal_fade not passed; dublin.odin:330 `dublin_node_block_draw :: proc(v: ^View, c: rl.Vector2, fam: rl.Color, reveal_scale: f32) -> f32 {` has no fade param; the sprite path (view.odin:1138) uses `{255, 255, 255, u8(255 * clamp01(reveal_fade))}` and draw_family_wash(v, dst, fam, reveal_fade).
detail: The v2-spawn-feel reveal (scale 0.4->1 + fade over 8 ticks) loses its fade half on Dublin: blocks appear fully opaque. Unspecified by this briefing but a silent regression of shipped presentation behavior.
recommended_fix: Add a reveal_fade parameter to dublin_node_block_draw and alpha-blend the block fill (and frontage edge) with it, matching the sprite path.

title: Baked street_blocks are unused by the game renderer — live re-derivation with different constants duplicates the logic and bloats dublin.json ~55%
evidence: osm_extract.py:89 `# (center + direction + size), so the render stays dumb.` and :760 `street_blocks = build_street_blocks(spawn, arterial, local)`; grep for street_blocks across core/, app/, harness/ returns nothing (exit 1). dublin.odin instead does a live nearest-segment search (`DUBLIN_SEG_MAX_DIST :: 3.0`, `DUBLIN_NODE_BLOCK_L :: 0.40`) while the bake uses BLOCK_SNAP_MAX_TILES = 0.6 and blen 0.34-0.39. dublin.json: 6,030,218 bytes vs 3,889,867 at v2.
detail: Two parallel street-block implementations (baked data for the mocks, live lookup in-game) with different snap radii and sizes can drift from the user-approved mock look; ~2 MB of game-loaded JSON is never read by the game.
recommended_fix: Pick one source of truth: either have dublin.odin consume the baked street_blocks (indexed like spawn_candidates) or drop street_blocks from the shipped asset and keep it bake-side only.

title: Committed bake tool defaults to machine-specific transient worktree paths — the committed underlay cannot be re-baked from a fresh clone
evidence: blender_board_build.py:15 `WT = os.environ.get("PP_WT") or "/Users/moses/.herdr/worktrees/packet-plumber/perkins-packet-plumber-v2-dublin-map-beautify"  # the packet-plumber root (PP_WT overrides)`; line 6 docstring: `exec(open("/Users/moses/.herdr/worktrees/packet-plumber/packet-plumber-v2-dublin-map-beautify/.scratch/blender_board_build.py").read())` — two different dead paths on any other checkout.
detail: PR claims 'the bake pipeline lives in tools/blender_board/ and is deterministic from the pinned raw cache'. Both default paths point at a transient herdr worktree, so the documented usage fails everywhere else; the two paths even disagree.
recommended_fix: Derive WT from __file__ (repo root = dirname(dirname(dirname(__file__)))) with PP_WT as an explicit override, and fix the docstring example.
